title: Additive functors commute with the bounded-below finite diagonals
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive functor between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let I be a double complex with degrees $(s,r)\in\mathbf Z\times\mathbf N$. Suppose that $I^{s,\bullet}=0$ for s below some integer b. Extend by zero and flip using [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation]. Write $J=(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(1_{\mathcal A})(I))^{\mathrm{flip}}$ and $J_F=(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(F)(I))^{\mathrm{flip}}$. There is a complex isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Tot}(J_F)\cong F(\operatorname{Tot}(J))$. On the $(m,s)$ diagonal summand in total degree n=m+s, its forward map composed with the inclusion is the extension identification from the F-mapped row to $F(I^{s,m})$, followed by F of the inverse extension identification and the inclusion into $\operatorname{Tot}(J)$. No left exactness or injectivity hypotheses are needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: additivity commutes with the finite diagonal sums

proof.text: For J, a summand in degree (r,s) vanishes if r<0 by extension by zero, or s<b by the lower bound. For fixed n define the finite diagonal indexing type $S_n=\{s\in\mathbf Z\mid b\le s\le n\}$ with maps $s\mapsto n-s$ and $s\mapsto s$. Every nonzero diagonal term occurs uniquely in this family. In Lean this is a CoreHasTotal witness. Additivity preserves the finite coproduct on this type, and CoreHasTotal.preserves extends this preservation to the entire diagonal by adding the zero terms. Hence F.PreservesTotalComplex holds for J.

Apply the source library HomologicalComplex₂.mapTotalIso to obtain $\operatorname{Tot}(F(J))\cong F(\operatorname{Tot}(J))$. HomologicalComplex.mapExtendIso gives the natural isomorphism between applying F after extension and extending after applying F. Lift it to complexes in the complex degree, flip it, and take its inverse, obtaining $J_F\cong F(J)$. Totalization of this bicomplex isomorphism followed by mapTotalIso is the required e.

For a natural resolution degree m, use the source library ιTotal_map equation and ι_mapTotalXIso_hom. The extension comparison at m is fixed by embeddingUpNat.r_f and mapExtendX_hom_eq. Expanding the two extension isomorphisms leaves composites of equality transports. Functoriality of those transports and eqToHom_trans give exactly the stipulated diagonal equation.
